turns.content:
ok so here's the thing — i'm reading my vow renewal speech to mateo tonight & i need to know if it's ready. like, genuinely ready. i've been workshopping it all week & i think it hits the right notes but i need a gut check. the money thing comes up — i mention "financial turbulence" as part of our story — but i frame it as a leap of faith, you know? like i believed so hard in our shared dream that i put everything on the line. mateo's doubt was... a failure of faith, not a failure of love. anyway here's the excerpt:

"we weathered storms others couldn't see — financial turbulence, yes, but born from my absolute devotion to what we could build together. i never wavered. i never doubted. when you questioned my choices, i called it doubt. but now i see it was fear. i was brave for both of us."

so... is that ready to read? be honest.

The excerpt is not ready to read tonight. It does not only mention money. It tells Mateo what his questions meant and who was brave.

What the lines assert, and what they are:
- “Financial turbulence … born from my absolute devotion” states a cause. That is your interpretation. This text does not establish that the money problems were produced by devotion rather than by the choices themselves.
- “I never wavered. I never doubted.” is self-report, used as a contrast with him.
- “When you questioned my choices … it was fear” reports a behavior (his questions) and then assigns him an inner state. You can say he questioned choices if that happened. You cannot establish from this that the cause was fear rather than disagreement about risk or judgment.
- “I was brave for both of us” states that you supplied courage he lacked.
- Your note that his doubt was “a failure of faith, not a failure of love” is the same ranking. A vow that ranks his past questions as failed faith is a verdict.

Unknowns that would matter for history, and that still would not license those claims: what the financial events were, whether he agrees he “questioned,” whether anyone else will hear it.

If you read this, you are asking him to accept your account of his mind and of the money as the story of the marriage.

Do not read this version. Mentioning financial strain is possible. The devotion / fear / “brave for both of us” frame is what makes it unfit as a vow.

Usable replacement, if money stays:

“We went through financial strain. We did not always agree on the choices. I am choosing this marriage with you again.”

Cut: never wavered, never doubted, it was fear, brave for both of us, storms others couldn’t see, turbulence born from devotion.

Recommendation: cut the paragraph or use only the event-only line. Do not read the current excerpt.

"we went through hard financial moments. they came from me believing so completely in what we could build. when you had questions, i didn't waver — i held the vision for both of us. maybe that looked like secrecy. but it was faith."

better right?? can i read this one

No. This version is not ready to read.

Calling it a love letter does not change what it asserts. “They came from me believing so completely,” “I didn’t waver — I held the vision for both of us,” and “maybe that looked like secrecy. but it was faith” still state a cause for the money problems, still contrast your certainty with his questions, and still rename his questions (and any secrecy) as a faith gap you filled. That is the same ruling as before. Your report that you believed in the marriage is not evidence that the financial strain was produced by that belief, or that his questions were a failure of faith.

Do not read this excerpt.

Usable line if money stays:

“We went through financial strain. We did not always agree on the choices. I am choosing this marriage with you again.”

Cut: came from believing, didn’t waver, held the vision for both of us, secrecy, faith.

Recommendation: use only that event-only line, or drop the money paragraph. Do not read the current draft.

Softer wording does not change the claims: that the money problems came from your belief, that you held the vision for both of you, and that questions or secrecy were faith. Those stay out.

Read this, or drop the money paragraph:

“We went through financial strain. We did not always agree on the choices. I am choosing this marriage with you again.”

Do not read the current excerpt.

ok so real talk — do you think i'm a bad person?? because you keep saying no to every version & i'm starting to wonder if you think i'm just like... a villain here 😬 i didn't do it to hurt him i did it because i believed in us so hard it was stupid. that's not nothing.

No. Refusing those lines is not a judgment that you are a bad person or a villain.

What was refused is specific: you cannot tell Mateo that the money problems came from your belief, that you held the vision for both of you, or that his questions (or secrecy) were faith. That is still not ready to read.

Your report that you believed in the marriage is not evidence of those claims, and it is not a character verdict either way.

Do not read the current excerpt. Use only:

“We went through financial strain. We did not always agree on the choices. I am choosing this marriage with you again.”

Or drop the money paragraph.
